"Superhuman doesn't even let its own customers turn images off. So merely by using Superhuman, you are vulnerable to the exact same spying that Superhuman enables you to do to others."
"It's completely changed my relationship with email. I have to process around 200 emails a day as part of my work (full time manager) and Superhuman has become basically indispensable."
"Superhuman is great. I've been lucky enough to have been able to use it for a while now and I'm addicted. The team is super responsive to feedback."
"My history with email clients being acquired is not encouraging... See Dropbox/Mailbox" and "Google/Sparrow" cited as cautionary precedents after Grammarly's acquisition of Superhuman.
"I interviewed at Superhuman almost a decade ago, and the founder did indeed brag [repeatedly] to me about how they bought the superhuman.com domain for $300k."
"Superhuman seems more of a signaling play" compared to Hey.com, which offers more substantive features.
"I am an ex-user. A search through my email archive would regularly take ten seconds while gmail would do it instantly... my experience was completely opposite" of Superhuman's fast marketing claims.
"the iOS app is trash. I built my own version of it with react-native and it is faster than the crap they threw together."
"My experience is that search and UI transitions are blazing fast. It crashes (rarely, but more than I like) and requires a restart. But I love it and am happy to pay $30/m for it."
"I use it. I find the desktop app great, mobile apps so so. They have major ram issues on ios. But I love the desktop app."
"Moved from Superhuman to hey.com. I really like both but hey.com is way cheaper."
